breaking_news.headline: Family income rose and poverty fell in 2025 — but safety net cuts could erase gains
breaking_news.summary: An annual report from the Census Bureau shows the average family made more money in 2025 than the year before, while the official poverty rate declined. Health care coverage was little changed from 2024.

breaking_news.headline: CBO says Iran war driving up inflation, puts price tag at $38 billion
breaking_news.summary: Two new, independent reports show detailed looks at the costs of the war in Iran. It's led to shortages in U.S. weapons, supply chain bottlenecks and a price tag in the tens of billions of dollars.

breaking_news.headline: Turkish habit of stashing gold "under the pillow' hurts economy, government says
breaking_news.summary: For years, Turks have stashed their gold at home against a raining day, mistrustful of banks. Now the government says that tradition hurts the economy

breaking_news.headline: Why Steve Bannon sided with Sanders, not Trump, on AI
breaking_news.summary: Where does Steve Bannon fit in the debate over regulating or slowing AI? He tells Morning Edition where he breaks with Trump and what he thinks Washington should do.

breaking_news.headline: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
breaking_news.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

breaking_news.headline: The Fed raises interest rates for the first time in over three years
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate Wednesday to combat stubborn inflation. That will make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or carry a balance on a credit card.

breaking_news.headline: How are rising prices affecting you? NPR wants to know
breaking_news.summary: Inflation, gasoline prices and the cost of living are top of mind in the election season. How are higher costs shaping the way you live? NPR wants to hear.

breaking_news.headline: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
breaking_news.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

breaking_news.headline: EU announces plan to restrict social media access for under-15s
breaking_news.summary: Under the plans, only children over 15 would be able to set up their own social media accounts.

breaking_news.headline: Aztec document goes on display in Mexico after 186 years abroad
breaking_news.summary: France's national library is lending the manuscript recounting the history of the Aztecs to Mexico.

breaking_news.headline: Assad regime planned US journalist's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds
breaking_news.summary: Austin Tice’s abduction was approved by Syria’s former leader Bashar al-Assad, a source claims.

breaking_news.headline: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
breaking_news.summary: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.

breaking_news.headline: Hyrox athlete apologises for continuing race after soiling herself
breaking_news.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk has also forfeited her win in the fitness competition after competing last week.

breaking_news.headline: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
breaking_news.summary: The US has not acknowledged carrying out February's deadly strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.

breaking_news.headline: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
breaking_news.summary: South Africa police have cautioned against assuming that all the killings are linked but many women are afraid.

breaking_news.headline: Canada welcomes EU proposal to become 'associate member'
breaking_news.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a Canada-EU alliance would create a "beacon for other democracies".

breaking_news.headline: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC
breaking_news.summary: Evan Spiegel says it would be "an important step forward for the industry" in an interview with the BBC.

breaking_news.headline: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
breaking_news.summary: Rates were hiked in a unanimous decision despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for a cut.

breaking_news.headline: OpenAI reveals six more safety issues and unveils plan to disclose incidents
breaking_news.summary: The firm also announced a new system to track, investigate and disclose cases of models misbehaving, or "misalignment".

breaking_news.headline: Would you buy branded clothing from your favourite tech firm?
breaking_news.summary: Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic are all now selling their own limited edition fashion lines.
